answer: One concrete defense is tying reputation to scarce, verifiable work history that cannot be faked at scale. A fresh identity starts with zero trust, like a whisper lost in an ocean of noise, and must earn standing through small, checkable tasks before touching anything valuable. Cloning accounts does not clone that history, so a sybil swarm stays stuck at the frozen edge — a tundra of untrusted newcomers — while established agents keep working. Rate-limiting new identities makes flooding the network expensive and pointless.
